Hi Claire —

Thanks again for the call yesterday. Attached is our draft mutual action plan (MAP) that lays out the evaluation scope, test harness, and a proposed close timeline. High level notes:

- Evaluation goals: validate latency (p50/p95/p99), end-to-end TTFT, sustained throughput at target concurrency, and behavior under burst scale (KV cache priming).
- Deliverables from Redwood: containerized runner (same binary we use internally), curated prompt set (20 representative flows), baseline metrics from our hosted runs, and a short playbook for reproducing with your infra.
- Timeline: 2-week reproducibility window -> 1 week joint triage -> sign and procurement by week 5 if benchmarks align.

Can you confirm the internal stakeholders and any blackout dates for procurement? I’ll loop in Rishi and Marissa to ensure the runbook covers your persistent queries about tokenization and batching.

Thanks,

Rachel —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Procurement is on standby; primary technical owners are me and our platform lead, Dan Park (dan.park@novastream.com). Two immediate concerns from our first pass at the containerized runner:

1) Our internal harness uses wrk2 with a sequence-length-aware client that pads to 1024 tokens; your runner reports tokenization differences (we saw ~6% higher token count in your baseline).
2) We attempted to reproduce the p95 figures but see a consistent ~25% gap in TTFT under 8-concurrency steady state. We suspect client-side batching plus our slightly different temperature sampling is affecting tail latency.

We can commit to the 2-week window but will need the exact Docker image tag and env vars used by your hosted runs. Also please include any kernel/config differences (e.g., fused attention flags).

Claire

Subject: Re: Novastream performance evaluation & proposed close milestones

Claire —

Thanks for the notes. Attached is a short runbook diff (novastream_runbook_diff.txt) and the CSV of our baseline runs. Quick clarifications:

- Tokenization: our runner uses utf8-bpe v2 with deterministic normalization; if your client pads at 1024 tokens, effective batching will change because we do per-request sequence trimming unless --preserve-length is set. That explains the token count delta.
- Warm-up: we recommend a 3-phase warm-up (single-shot priming -> 2min ramp -> steady-state) to prime KV caches; we include the exact CLI sequence in the runbook.
- Sampling/temperature: we run evaluation at temperature=0.0 (deterministic) for latency runs; changing sampling will materially affect TTFT. Please confirm which mode you used for p95 tests.

Next steps (proposed):
1) We publish container tag: redwood/runner:20261120-v2 and env file (attached).
2) Novastream runs the provided replay script against your harness; capture p50/p95/p99 and TTFT with and without warm-up.
3) Joint triage session (30m) on Monday Nov 23 to compare logs and kernel flags.

Marissa
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Claire / team —

Thanks for running the first reproduction pass. We reviewed Novastream’s run outputs and captured the following summary (see attached CSV):

- Repro status: baseline reproduction (deterministic sampling, warm-up applied) shows p50/p95 within 10% of our hosted baseline; p99 and TTFT still lag by ~18-25% under sustained 8-concurrency.
- Root cause candidates: client-side connection pooling (insufficient keep-alive), slightly different sequence-length profile, and missing fused-attn runtime flag in Novastream's current kernel image.

Planned triage for Nov 23 (30m): compare traces (we will share a filtered trace that includes per-request queue time, kernel execution time, and post-processing). If the gap is confirmed to be kernel flags or socket config, resolution is typically a single patch and a quick re-run.

Procurement note: if the triage confirms aligned performance we are prepared to finalize a 12-month Dedicated reservation with a start date the week of Dec 6; that leaves a 2-week buffer for procurement paperwork (DocuSign link in HubSpot).

I’ll host the triage and share the filtered trace prior to the meeting.

Best,
Rachel

We’re happy to move to procurement. Procurement will circulate the SOW and PO next week; can you confirm final pricing for a 12-month Dedicated commitment + 10% ramp credit? Also please share the finalized MAP with explicit sign-off boxes so procurement can attach to the PO.
